sentences.text: The skull's upper profile is smooth and slightly concave, lacking any bony crests, while the lower jaws are long and lack a keel.
The front teeth differ in length from one another, are very elongated and pointed, and generally increase strongly in length toward the front while becoming more directed anteriorly.
The underside of the lower jaw symphysis features a trough, and the lower jaw is 174 millimeters long and contains about twenty-seven teeth.
The generic name comes from Greek and Latin words meaning 'wing' and 'filter' or 'felt', referring to the animal's teeth.
The holotype fossil dates to the early Aptian, approximately 125 million years old.
The genus Pterofiltrus was named by Jiang Shunxing and Wang Xiaolin in 2011, with the type species being Pterofiltrus qiui, which honors Professor Qiu Zhanxiang.

The holotype fossil was found in the early 21st century at Zhangjiagou, Liaoning Province, in rocks dating to about 125 million years ago, and consists of a disarticulated skull, parts of a hyoid bone, and the first two neck vertebrae.
Phylogenetic analysis recovered Pterofiltrus as the sister taxon of Gladocephaloideus within the Ctenochasmatidae.
Pterofiltrus lived during the Early Cretaceous in western Liaoning, China, from the Barremian to the Aptian, between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.
